lithology.official_description: Upper etched unit—Indurated, rugged, moderately cratered to heavily cratered, light- to intermediate-toned unit located along and on the northern Jezero crater rim and wall, along the interior margin of Jezero crater, and throughout Nili Planum. Overlies units Nnp1 and cr in Nili Planum and conformably overlies unit Nle in Jezero crater. Contains three different surface textures with varying morphologic and erosional textures that grade into one another without clear or systematic stratigraphic contacts: a ridged surface in northern Jezero and northeastern Nili Planum, a heavily cratered surface in northern Nili Planum, and a light-toned rugged surface in southern Nili Planum (fig. 3). Type localities: lat 18.67° N., long 77.57° E.
lithology.interpretation: Official geomorphological map unit; no inferred quantitative mineral abundance.

lithology.official_description: Eolian bedform unit—Light-toned, linear, commonly parallel, low-relief ridges prevalent in local topographic lows, such as impact craters, including along the interior margin of Jezero crater and at the base of steep scarps throughout Nili Planum. Superposes other map units. Type locality: lat 18.41° N., long 77.36° E.
lithology.interpretation: Official geomorphological map unit; no inferred quantitative mineral abundance.

lithology.official_description: Jezero fan unit 2—Lightly cratered, intermediate-toned, stratified unit with margins defined by sharp scarps, located at the mouth of Neretva Vallis in the western Jezero crater floor. Occurs at higher elevation than unit NHjf1 (lat 18.58° N., long 77.48° E.). Contains rugged arcuate ridges and troughs that branch out from nodes and define several overlapping lobes (fig. 7). Meter-scale sequences of alternating light and dark strata, as well as some curvilinear strata (lat 18.48° N., long 77.39° E.; lat 18.47° N., long 77.37° E.). Forms isolated outcrops that are <50 m in height on the Jezero crater floor east of the main unit. Some outcrops exhibit parallel stratification on their slopes (lat 18.43° N., long 77.36° E.), while others do not exhibit obvious visible stratification at map scale (for example, lat 18.47° N., long 77.50° E.). Type localities: lat 18.49° N., long 77.36° E.
lithology.interpretation: Official geomorphological map unit; no inferred quantitative mineral abundance.

lithology.official_description: Crater rim unit—Rugged, light- to intermediate-toned, relatively high relief scarps surrounding circular or quasicircular depressions >500 m in diameter. Type locality: lat 18.04° N., long 77.51° E.
lithology.interpretation: Official geomorphological map unit; no inferred quantitative mineral abundance.

lithology.official_description: Jezero floor unit—Rugged, moderately to heavily cratered, light- to dark-toned, planar unit with margins defined by low-relief, sharp, lobate scarps. Forms central portion of Jezero crater floor and overlies and embays units Nue and Nle, respectively. Most impact craters on this surface are <200 m in diameter. May have dark, smooth surface texture, especially near contact with unit NHjf2. Type locality: lat 18.43° N., long 77.65° E.
lithology.interpretation: Official geomorphological map unit; no inferred quantitative mineral abundance.

lithology.official_description: Lower etched unit—Rugged, lightly cratered, light- to intermediate-toned unit concentrically exposed on floor of Jezero adjacent to unit Njf. Type locality: lat 18.28° N., long 77.49° E.
